title: Starship Flight 14 Clears Wet Dress Rehearsal
detail: SpaceX completed a wet dress rehearsal (WDR) for Starship Flight 14 at Starbase on September 24, 2026, loading Booster 21 and Ship 41 with thousands of tons of cryogenic propellant and running the countdown sequence down to just short of engine ignition before draining the vehicle back down. SpaceX posted on X that the 'launch rehearsal' was 'complete ahead of Starship Flight 14.' The test clears one of the final major technical hurdles before the vehicle's first orbital attempt; the 75-minute launch window opens 7:15am-8:30am CT Monday, September 28 from Starbase. SpaceX still requires an FAA launch license, which had not been issued as of the rehearsal's completion. Flight 14 will attempt a six-orbit, ~275km, near-10-hour mission deploying 26 Starlink V3 satellites, with Super Heavy targeting an offshore Gulf of Mexico landing and Ship 41 a Pacific Ocean splashdown near Chile.

media.caption: Starship Flight 14's stacked vehicle at sunset at Starbase after clearing its wet dress rehearsal

title: Google Confirms Project Suncatcher AI Satellite Will Fly on SpaceX Transporter-18
detail: Google confirmed its prototype Project Suncatcher satellite — carrying four Trillium Tensor Processing Units built in partnership with Earth-imaging company Planet — will launch on SpaceX's Transporter-18 rideshare mission from Vandenberg Space Force Base on October 1, 2026, targeting a dawn-dusk sun-synchronous orbit. The refrigerator-sized 'MVP' satellite is a research test of whether low Earth orbit — where satellites can generate up to eight times more solar power than ground systems — could eventually support scalable machine-learning infrastructure. Testing will assess the TPUs' survival of 50-100g launch loads, radiation resistance (the chips already passed a UC Davis proton-beam test exceeding five years' expected ionizing dose), and in-vacuum thermal management. Google says a two-satellite laser-link communication test is planned for 2027, with a longer-term vision of orbital clusters of TPU chips linked by high-bandwidth lasers.

media.caption: Google's Project Suncatcher prototype satellite, carrying four TPUs, is set to fly on SpaceX's Transporter-18 rideshare Oct 1
